pages.text:
Heats a receiver with the sun: up to 600 HU/t at 1,100°C at clear noon. The temperature follows the sun: above 500°C (High-Pressure Steam) from about 7:45 to 16:15 in clear weather, and above 900°C (a Superheater Array, or Superheated Steam) from about 9:40 to 14:20.
# Building
A 2x2 tower 4 tall: three layers of Solar Thermal Array Casings with one controller in the bottom layer, facing out, and four Solar Collectors on top. Formed, it becomes a tower with a trough mirror on top that follows the sun.
The controller's facing is the tracking axis: north or south for the north-south axis (full output), east or west for east-west (x0.7).

# Sun and weather
The alpha follows the sun's height and uses the source rain/thunder multipliers. Each collector without full sky light contributes no output. Horizon's pinned hooks do not expose Arcforge's biome tags or distinguish snow from rain, so alpha uses a neutral biome multiplier and treats precipitation as rain. The controller records its stowed state during thunderstorms, but animated trough stowing is not implemented.
# Heat out
A new tower has no heat-output faces enabled. Use the Wrench on a formed tower part and click the face touching a supported heat machine or thermal conduit to toggle that face's heat output. Enabled faces push stored heat to supported machines or into the conduit. To continue a run, configure each thermal conduit face with the Wrench: Auto permits either direction, Input receives, Output sends, and Disabled disconnects. Thermal transfer uses per-segment limits rather than Arcforge's pooled network rate. Enabled faces show a standard blockstate collar and heat-port plate; the source dynamic nozzle depth is not reproduced.
One array gives less heat than a boiler can boil, so set the boiler's pressure to High-Pressure to hold it at 500°C.
